description:
verify.rs delegates all cryptographic verification through `pkix_path::SignatureVerifier`. pkix-ct itself contains zero algorithm-specific code; the TLS-tag → X.509-OID map (`tls_alg_to_x509_oid`) is the only algorithm-aware code, and it's pure data.

A future contributor might suggest:
- 'pkix-ct should bring its own ECDSA backend, since CT logs almost always use P-256.'
- 'The SignatureVerifier trait is overkill for the simple case.'

Both suggestions should be rejected. The whole point of pkix-path's SignatureVerifier trait (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #3: 'SignatureVerifier is the only place algorithm-specific code lives in pkix-path') is that the same algorithm-backend choices apply across the workspace. pkix-ct inheriting that decision automatically is the correct architecture. The fact that pkix-ct ended up with zero algo code is the validation that the abstraction works.

Also defend: the duplication of OID constants in verify.rs:91-99 (rather than re-exporting from pkix-path). The author's comment at verify.rs:86-89 explains: pkix-path's copies are private and feature-gated. Re-exporting them would force a feature dependency that pkix-ct doesn't actually have. Acceptable trade.
title: Algorithm dispatch via pkix-path::SignatureVerifier — keeps pkix-ct algo-agnostic
